_comment: Cards for the root README, built with readme-forge-design/scripts/make_page.py. readme-cards.md is the generated snippet list; README.md places the cards by hand between its real headings.

blocks.prompt: ~ $ /readme-forge write a README for this repo
blocks.greeting: Your code is the source of truth.
blocks.title: readme-forge
blocks.alt: readme-forge: Your code is the source of truth. Your README should be too. A Claude skill for verified READMEs, Python 3.8+, standard library only.

items.title: verify_readme.py
items.subtitle: every claim, checked against the repo
items.description: Checks commands, package-manager scripts, CLI flags, env vars and paths. What it can't check offline is reported as unverifiable, never as correct.

items.title: analyze_repo.py
items.subtitle: facts, not guesses
items.description: Reads manifests, lockfiles, scripts, env vars, Docker, CI and routes.

items.title: import_graph.py
items.subtitle: diagrams from real imports
items.description: Drafts a Mermaid diagram from imports in Python, JS/TS, Go and Rust.

items.title: score_readme.py
items.subtitle: score, lint and drift
items.description: Grades structure, accessibility, links and drift, and flags commands that no longer match.

items.title: Every platform
items.subtitle: one source, many READMEs
items.description: GitHub, Hugging Face cards with validated YAML, and PyPI, npm and GitLab ports.

items.title: The score, tested
items.subtitle: 25 well-regarded vs 25 neglected READMEs
items.description: Pinned to commit SHAs. The rubric still rewards headings over content, so use it as a checklist, not a verdict.

blocks.title: Ship the README.
blocks.alt: Every claim checked. Ship the README. MIT License, made with readme-forge.
